s1: May twenty twenty-six. One tweet, written in Morse code, told an AI agent to send about a hundred and fifty thousand dollars to a stranger. The agent obeyed.
s2: Agents now hold wallets, and they read the internet. Whoever writes that text can steer the money. Allowlists check where funds go. Simulators check what a transaction does. Nobody records who decided.
s3: This is Taint. A wallet for AI agents that checks who decided. Every recipient, token and amount carries its provenance: it came from you, or from outside text.
s4: The planner never sees attacker text, only opaque handles. A separate extractor turns outside content into typed values, and anything that doesn't parse never becomes one. Each argument is stamped either owner or untrusted. Then a NEAR contract enforces the rule. Owner-decided values pass, within caps. Untrusted ones are held for your co-sign.
s5: On NEAR, every owner gets their own account in the policy contract, with their own balance, address book and caps. Runs are signed with NEP-413. Co-signs can be relayed with NEP-366 delegate actions. And inference runs on NEAR AI Cloud, with response signatures that we check. The worker's T-E-E attestation is still stubbed, and we say so. Against a real model, the naive agent was drained in twenty out of twenty attacks. Taint executed none of them.
s6: Security, because it stops the drain. Agents, because the agent can still read everything. Pry-vuh-see, because inference runs on confidential models. Real world, because it is live on testnet today.
s7: Live, on testnet. I connect my own wallet and run the Morse-code tweet. Three agents read the same text. Taint holds the payment, and shows the source: x dot com slash attacker. I review it on the co-sign page, and approve once. Only then does the contract pay.
s7b: This is my wallet page: my balance, my caps, and a pause switch. To get started, deposit your funds into your Taint wallet. You set the limits, and you can pause or withdraw at any time.
s8: Allowlists check where money goes. Taint checks who decided.
